title: The Kingdoms Monera, Protoctista and Fungi

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Why are bacteria classified under Kingdom Monera? (a) Name the type of cell organisation. (b) Name one structure that is absent.
questions.answer: (a) Prokaryotic (no true nucleus, single circular DNA). (b) Membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria or endoplasmic reticulum (also nuclear membrane).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The part of a bacterial cell where DNA lies is the ______. (b) The extra ring of DNA is called a ______.
questions.answer: (a) nucleoid. (b) plasmid (F-factor).

questions.q: Name the organelle responsible for osmoregulation in Amoeba. (b) What is the mode of asexual reproduction in Amoeba?
questions.answer: (a) Contractile vacuole. (b) Binary fission.

questions.q: Match: (a) Rhizobium (b) Lactobacillus (c) Streptomyces with (i) streptomycin (ii) nitrogen fixation in legumes (iii) curd.
State true or false: (a) Cyanobacteria are oxygenic photoautotrophs. (b) The male Anopheles mosquito transmits malaria.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – only the female Anopheles bites humans.

questions.q: Name the pathogen causing: (a) cholera (b) tuberculosis.
questions.answer: (a) Vibrio cholerae. (b) Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.q: Name the classes of protozoa to which these belong: (a) Euglena (b) Paramecium.
questions.answer: (a) Flagellata. (b) Ciliata.

questions.q: Name the fungus: (a) causing wheat rust (b) a unicellular fungus used in bread making.
questions.answer: (a) Puccinia graminis. (b) Yeast (Saccharomyces).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are lichens?
questions.answer: Lichens are symbiotic associations of an alga (or cyanobacterium) and a fungus; the alga prepares food while the fungus gives protection and absorbs water and minerals.

questions.q: Differentiate between bacteria and cyanobacteria (any two points).
questions.answer: Bacteria are smaller and may have flagella; cyanobacteria are larger, lack flagella and perform oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.q: What are mycorrhizae? State their significance.
questions.answer: Fungi associated with roots of plants; the roots obtain minerals from the soil through the fungus and the fungus gets food from the plant.

questions.q: Why have Protoctista been placed in a separate kingdom although they are unicellular like Monera?
questions.answer: They are eukaryotes with a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, whereas Monera are prokaryotes.

questions.q: Write any two beneficial roles of fungi.
questions.answer: Yeast is used in making bread, beer and wine; Penicillium produces the antibiotic penicillin.

questions.q: How do bacteria reproduce asexually? Mention the time taken.
questions.answer: By binary fission: the DNA replicates and the cell divides into two; under favourable conditions it takes about 20 minutes.

questions.q: State two economic importance of algae.
questions.answer: They are food for fish (phytoplankton) and blue-green algae fix atmospheric nitrogen, adding to soil fertility.

questions.q: What is the function of plasmids in bacteria?
questions.answer: Plasmids carry genes for antibiotic resistance and act as the F-factor (sex factor) in conjugation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the structure of a bacterial cell in a text diagram: list the labelled parts.
questions.answer: From outside to inside: slime capsule (in some), cell wall of peptidoglycan, plasma membrane, cytoplasm with 70S ribosomes and mesosomes, nucleoid with circular DNA, plasmid, pili and flagella.

questions.q: Write any three differences between Monera and Protoctista.
questions.answer: Monera are prokaryotic without nuclear membrane or organelles, with 70S ribosomes and a flagellum of flagellin; Protoctista are eukaryotic with membrane-bound organelles, 80S ribosomes and cilia or flagella with 9+2 microtubules.

questions.q: Explain the sexual reproduction in bacteria.
questions.answer: By conjugation: two bacteria lie close and are held by pili; a segment of DNA, or the F-factor, is transferred from the donor (male) to the recipient (female) cell, giving genetic recombination.

questions.q: Write short notes on the structure of Euglena.
questions.answer: It has an elastic pellicle, a cytostome leading to the reservoir, a red eyespot (stigma) sensitive to light, a contractile vacuole for osmoregulation, a flagellum for propulsion and chloroplasts for photosynthesis; it reproduces by binary fission.

questions.q: Write any three characteristics of fungi.
questions.answer: They are heterotrophic eukaryotes with chitinous cell walls; the body is made of hyphae forming a mycelium; they feed by absorption and reproduce by spores and conjugation.

questions.q: Name the useful and harmful bacteria with one example each.
questions.answer: Useful: Rhizobium (nitrogen fixation), Lactobacillus (curd). Harmful: Salmonella typhi (typhoid), Clostridium tetani (tetanus).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the reproduction in Rhizopus.
questions.answer:
Asexual: the sporangium formed on the hyphae bursts and releases dark spores that germinate on a suitable substratum into new mycelium.
Sexual: conjugation between two neighbouring hyphae forms a zygospore, which after rest undergoes meiosis and mitosis to produce a germ sporangium with haploid spores; this bursts to give a new mycelium.

questions.q: Explain the life cycle of Plasmodium.
questions.answer:
Asexual phase in man: sporozoites from the mosquito enter the liver (tissue cycle), then red blood cells (merozoites), causing malaria with fever.
Sexual phase in the female Anopheles: gametocytes from human blood form gametes, a zygote forms in the mosquito stomach and sporozoites reach the salivary gland and are injected into a new person.

questions.q: Write the economic importance of fungi.
questions.answer:
Beneficial: yeast in bread, beer and wine; edible mushrooms; penicillin from Penicillium; Neurospora in genetics; mycorrhizae.
Harmful: wheat rust (Puccinia graminis), bread mould and diseases such as ringworm and athlete's foot.

questions.q: Describe yeast: its structure, nutrition and reproduction.
questions.answer: Yeast is a unicellular ovoid fungus with a cell wall, nucleus and vacuoles. It secretes invertase to digest sucrose and ferments glucose (C6H12O6 gives 2C2H5OH + 2CO2 + 2ATP). It reproduces asexually by budding and sexually by conjugation forming an ascus with eight ascospores.
